changes.before: A deliberately invalid label-timing control retains the original selected parameters, long history and refit clock on predetermined first, middle and last complete blocks: 72 FX origins and 39 Treasury origins. Replacing the clean pool ending at r−H with one ending at r includes 6 immature labels per refit. In Treasury QR the illegal oracle reduces loss by 33.3988% but changes breaches from 5 to 6; FX QR instead raises loss by 0.0639%. The complete QR, KNN and F outcomes in Supplement Table S37 have mixed directions. This post-result / exploratory control quantifies timing contamination in these blocks, not an inevitable optimism bias or an all-sample performance effect.

changes.before: Kupiec (1995) proportion-of-failures and Christoffersen (1998) independence/conditional-coverage diagnostics use the original first-origin-plus-j(H+1) grid. Conditional coverage here adds full-sample-grid POF to the transition-independence LR. A DQ-type full-sample HAC Wald adaptation of Engle and Manganelli (2004) uses the intercept, issue-known capacity and matured hit lags H+1 through H+4. Singular covariance or an unidentified transition row yields NA. The fixed 72-member common-history family receives Holm (1979) adjustment; exact identical losses use conservative p=1 solely for multiplicity bookkeeping. Supplement S9 and the output CSVs retain all statistics and statuses. The additional benchmarks in Supplement S16 use a separately stated transition-conditional CC likelihood on adjacent sparse-grid pairs, conditioning on the initial hit; their values do not replace this archived convention. Their ranking families are frozen separately, and NA adjustment bookkeeping is kept distinct from an observed p-value.
